```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Koele_2025_bedaquiline_QTcTBT"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1093/jac/dkaf210> (open access; PMC12313457)
* Supplement: Tables S1-S6, Figures S1-S3 and the NONMEM code (Text S1), at the
  same address.

Koele 2025 pooled the weekly ECGs of two phase IIb dose-finding trials in
drug-susceptible pulmonary tuberculosis, SUDOCU (sutezolid) and PanACEA DECODE
(delpazolid). Every arm received standard-dose bedaquiline, delamanid and
moxifloxacin, with or without one of four doses of the new oxazolidinone. The
paper fitted a population model to the QT interval corrected by a TB-specific
time-varying formula (QTcTBT), and refitted it to the Fridericia-corrected QTcF
as a sensitivity analysis. Both fits are packaged:

| Model | Endpoint | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `Koele_2025_bedaquiline_QTcTBT` | QTcTBT (primary) | Table 2, Text S1 |
| `Koele_2025_bedaquiline_QTcF` | QTcF (sensitivity) | Table S4 |

Both are step functions in time: the QTc is the individual baseline until day
10 of treatment and baseline plus a constant increase afterwards. Female sex and
age shift the baseline, and the day-14 AUC0-24 of the bedaquiline metabolite M2
shifts the increase. No exposure-response was found for sutezolid, delpazolid,
bedaquiline, delamanid or moxifloxacin (Table S3), so the model has no PK part.

# Population

`r readModelDb("Koele_2025_bedaquiline_QTcTBT")()$population$n_subjects`
adults (73 in SUDOCU, 76 in DECODE) with newly diagnosed smear-positive
drug-susceptible pulmonary TB, recruited in Tanzania and South Africa
(Koele 2025 Table 1). 76.5% were male, median age 33 (SUDOCU) and 34 (DECODE)
years (range 20-58), median weight 53 kg (40-84), and 13 were living with HIV.
Pre-existing cardiac disease, a QTcF above 450 ms and QT-prolonging
co-medication were exclusion criteria. The 2373 ECG observations were recorded
weekly between 8 and 10 AM, before the daily dose, after 10 min of supine rest.
Treatment lasted 12 weeks in SUDOCU and 16 weeks in DECODE.

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Koele_2025_bedaquiline_QTcTBT")()$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment pointing to its source. The
QTcTBT values are the `$THETA`, `$OMEGA` and `$SIGMA` records of Text S1, which
reproduce every Table 2 estimate; the QTcF values are from Table S4.

| Quantity | QTcTBT model | QTcF model | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline, male, 34 years (`lrbase`) | log(400) ms | log(388) ms | Table 2 / Table S4 |
| Increase from day 10 (`emax`) | 13.2 ms | 21.8 ms | Table 2 / Table S4 |
| Female sex on baseline (`e_sexf_rbase`) | 13.5 ms | 11.8 ms | Table 2 / Table S4 |
| Age on baseline (`e_age_rbase`), centred at 34 y | 0.367 ms/y | 0.391 ms/y | Table 2 / Table S4; centring Text S1 |
| M2 AUC0-24 on the increase (`e_auc_bedaquiline_m2_emax`), centred at 10.54 mg*h/L | 0.783 | 0.850 ms per mg*h/L | Table 2 / Table S4; centring Text S1 |
| IIV baseline, exponential (`etalrbase`) | 0.00162 | 0.0018473 | Text S1 `$OMEGA BLOCK(2)` / Table S4 4.30% |
| IIV increase, `TV * (1 + eta)` (`etaemax`) | 0.481 | 0.17330 | Text S1 / Table S4 43.5% |
| Covariance baseline-increase | -0.0136 | -0.0086063 | Text S1 / Table S4 correlation -48.1% |
| IIV on the timepoint residual (`eta_re_add`) | 0.225 | 0.19728 | Text S1 / Table S4 46.7% |
| IIV on the replicate residual (`eta_re_repl`) | 0.155 | 0.18067 | Text S1 / Table S4 44.5% |
| Timepoint residual SD (`addSd`) | sqrt(77) = 8.775 ms | 9.41 ms | Text S1 `$SIGMA` / Table S4 |
| Replicate residual SD (`addSdRepl`) | sqrt(24.2) = 4.919 ms | 4.48 ms | Text S1 `$SIGMA BLOCK(1)` / Table S4 |
| Step at `TIME > 10` days | | | Text S1 `IF(TIME.GT.10)` |
| `Y = IPRED + ERR(1)*EXP(ETA(3)) + repERR*EXP(ETA(4))` | | | Text S1 |

Table 2 and Table S4 print the variances as a coefficient of variation,
`100 * sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1)`, even for the increase, whose random effect is
additive-proportional. The check below shows that this convention reproduces
Table 2 from the Text S1 omegas; the QTcF omegas were obtained by inverting the
same formula.

```{r cv-convention}
cv <- function(omega2) 100 * sqrt(exp(omega2) - 1)
tab2 <- tibble::tibble(
  quantity = c("IIV baseline", "IIV increase", "IIV timepoint error", "IIV replicate error"),
  omega2 = c(0.00162, 0.481, 0.225, 0.155),
  table2_cv = c(4.00, 78.6, 50.2, 40.9)
) |>
  mutate(cv_from_code = cv(omega2))
knitr::kable(tab2, digits = 3)
corr_tbt <- -0.0136 / sqrt(0.00162 * 0.481)
stopifnot(
  all(abs(tab2$cv_from_code - tab2$table2_cv) < 0.06),
  abs(corr_tbt - (-0.487)) < 0.001
)
```

# The QTcTBT correction

The endpoint itself is a correction of the measured QT by the measured RR
interval, with an exponent that moves from Olliaro's 0.4081 before treatment
towards Fridericia's 1/3 as the disease-related tachycardia of untreated TB
resolves (Koele 2025 Methods, with TAST the time after the start of treatment in
weeks):

`QTcTBT = QT / RR^(0.4081 - 0.0781 * (1 - exp(-log(2) * TAST / 7.74)))`

The paper writes RR in ms; the power-law corrections only return a QT-sized
value when RR is in seconds (equivalently RR / 1000 ms), which is how the
helper below uses it.

```{r qtctbt-correction}
qtc_tbt <- function(qt_ms, rr_s, tast_wk) {
  qt_ms / rr_s^(0.4081 - 0.0781 * (1 - exp(-log(2) * tast_wk / 7.74)))
}
exponent <- function(tast_wk) 0.4081 - 0.0781 * (1 - exp(-log(2) * tast_wk / 7.74))
stopifnot(
  abs(exponent(0) - 0.4081) < 1e-12,
  # The exponent halves its way to Fridericia's 0.33 after 7.74 weeks.
  abs(exponent(7.74) - (0.4081 - 0.0781 / 2)) < 1e-12,
  abs(exponent(1e4) - 0.33) < 1e-6
)
# A QT of 330 ms at a heart rate of 110 bpm before treatment.
qtc_tbt(330, 60 / 110, 0)
```

# Typical-value checks

`rxode2::zeroRe()` removes all random effects; the output column `QTcTBT` is
then the closed-form prediction. Each covariate profile is evaluated before
(day 5) and after (day 20) the step.

```{r typical}
mod_tbt <- readModelDb("Koele_2025_bedaquiline_QTcTBT")
mod_f <- readModelDb("Koele_2025_bedaquiline_QTcF")

profiles <- tibble::tribble(
  ~profile, ~SEXF, ~AGE, ~AUC_BEDAQUILINE_M2,
  "Reference: male, 34 y, M2 AUC 10.54", 0, 34, 10.54,
  "Female", 1, 34, 10.54,
  "Age 50 years", 0, 50, 10.54,
  "M2 AUC 20 mg*h/L", 0, 34, 20
) |>
  mutate(id = row_number())
ev_typ <- tidyr::crossing(profiles, time = c(5, 20)) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = NA_character_) |>
  arrange(id, time)

typ_tbt <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_tbt), events = ev_typ,
                           keep = c("SEXF", "AGE", "AUC_BEDAQUILINE_M2")) |>
  as.data.frame()
typ_f <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_f), events = ev_typ,
                         keep = c("SEXF", "AGE", "AUC_BEDAQUILINE_M2")) |>
  as.data.frame()

closed_form <- function(time, SEXF, AGE, AUC, base, inc, sexf, age, m2) {
  base + sexf * SEXF + age * (AGE - 34) + (time > 10) * (inc + m2 * (AUC - 10.54))
}
typ_tbt$expected <- with(typ_tbt, closed_form(time, SEXF, AGE, AUC_BEDAQUILINE_M2,
                                              400, 13.2, 13.5, 0.367, 0.783))
typ_f$expected <- with(typ_f, closed_form(time, SEXF, AGE, AUC_BEDAQUILINE_M2,
                                          388, 21.8, 11.8, 0.391, 0.850))
stopifnot(
  max(abs(typ_tbt$QTcTBT - typ_tbt$expected)) < 1e-8,
  max(abs(typ_f$QTcF - typ_f$expected)) < 1e-8
)

typ_tbt |>
  select(id, time, QTcTBT) |>
  left_join(select(typ_f, id, time, QTcF), by = c("id", "time")) |>
  left_join(select(profiles, id, profile), by = "id") |>
  select(profile, time, QTcTBT, QTcF) |>
  dplyr::rename("Covariate profile" = profile, "Day" = time,
                "QTcTBT (ms)" = QTcTBT, "QTcF (ms)" = QTcF) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

The Discussion of Koele 2025 contrasts the two corrections for the typical
patient: a QTcF baseline of 388 ms and increase of 21.8 ms against 400 ms and
13.2 ms with QTcTBT. Fridericia under-corrects the high pre-treatment heart
rate, so it starts lower and appears to rise more.

```{r typical-contrast}
ref_tbt <- typ_tbt |> filter(id == 1)
ref_f <- typ_f |> filter(id == 1)
stopifnot(
  abs(diff(ref_tbt$QTcTBT) - 13.2) < 1e-8,
  abs(diff(ref_f$QTcF) - 21.8) < 1e-8,
  abs(ref_tbt$QTcTBT[1] - ref_f$QTcF[1] - 12) < 1e-8
)
```

# Virtual cohort

The individual data are not public. The cohort below reproduces the design of
each study: weekly single ECGs from the start of treatment to week 12 (SUDOCU)
or week 16 (DECODE), with sex, age and M2 exposure drawn to match Table 1 and
Tables S5-S6. Age is drawn from a normal distribution around the 34-year median
clipped to the observed 20-58 range; M2 AUC0-24 from a log-normal around the
10.54 mg*h/L median whose spread covers the 3.5-23.5 range of the arm tables.
150 virtual subjects per study, within the 200-per-arm cap.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2025)
n_per_study <- 150L
make_study <- function(study, n, female_frac, last_week, id0) {
  tibble::tibble(
    id = id0 + seq_len(n),
    study = study,
    SEXF = rbinom(n, 1, female_frac),
    AGE = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, 34, 9), 20), 58),
    AUC_BEDAQUILINE_M2 = 10.54 * exp(rnorm(n, 0, 0.3))
  ) |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = 7 * (0:last_week))
}
cohort <- bind_rows(
  make_study("SUDOCU", n_per_study, 19 / 73, 12, 0L),
  make_study("DECODE", n_per_study, 16 / 76, 16, n_per_study)
) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = NA_character_) |>
  arrange(id, time)
```

# Simulation

The stochastic solve draws every random effect, including the two
residual-error random effects; the `sim` column holds the simulated ECG reading
and `QTcTBT` the individual prediction.

```{r simulate}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2025)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_tbt, events = cohort,
                       keep = c("study", "SEXF", "AGE", "AUC_BEDAQUILINE_M2")) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(week = time / 7)
```

# Replicate Figure 3 (VPC)

Figure 3 of Koele 2025 overlays the 2.5th, 50th and 97.5th percentiles of the
observed QTcTBT on the model-simulated percentiles for each study. The
reference values in the figure below were read from Figure 3 by the maintainers
(approximate, to about 3 ms): the median rises from about 403-405 ms at the
start of treatment to about 413-420 ms (SUDOCU) and 415-424 ms (DECODE), and
the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles sit at about 380-395 ms and 443-458 ms on
treatment.

```{r figure-3, fig.height = 4.5}
pct <- sim |>
  group_by(study, week) |>
  summarise(
    p025 = quantile(sim, 0.025),
    p50 = quantile(sim, 0.5),
    p975 = quantile(sim, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(study = factor(study, levels = c("SUDOCU", "DECODE")))

fig3_ref <- tibble::tribble(
  ~study, ~lo, ~hi, ~percentile,
  "SUDOCU", 413, 420, "50th",
  "SUDOCU", 380, 395, "2.5th",
  "SUDOCU", 443, 458, "97.5th",
  "DECODE", 415, 424, "50th",
  "DECODE", 380, 392, "2.5th",
  "DECODE", 443, 455, "97.5th"
) |>
  mutate(study = factor(study, levels = c("SUDOCU", "DECODE")))

ggplot(pct, aes(week)) +
  geom_rect(data = fig3_ref, aes(xmin = 2, xmax = Inf, ymin = lo, ymax = hi),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "grey80", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "firebrick", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p025), colour = "steelblue", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(aes(y = p975), colour = "steelblue", linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~study) +
  labs(x = "Time after start of treatment (weeks)", y = "QTcTBT (ms)",
       caption = paste("Lines: simulated 2.5th, 50th and 97.5th percentiles (150 subjects per study).",
                       "Grey bands: on-treatment ranges read from Koele 2025 Figure 3.",
                       sep = "\n")) +
  theme_bw()
```

The on-treatment percentiles from week 2 onwards are checked against the
Figure 3 ranges, widened for the reading accuracy and for the cohort-to-cohort
spread of a 150-subject simulation: by 5 ms for the median and 10 ms for the
2.5th and 97.5th percentiles, which move more between cohorts.

```{r figure-3-check}
on_trt <- sim |>
  filter(week >= 2) |>
  group_by(study) |>
  summarise(p025 = quantile(sim, 0.025), p50 = median(sim), p975 = quantile(sim, 0.975))
baseline <- sim |> filter(week == 0) |> summarise(p50 = median(sim))
knitr::kable(on_trt, digits = 1)
# Over three cohort seeds the simulated values were 415.6-418.1 (median),
# 372.8-380.8 (2.5th), 456.6-461.7 (97.5th) and 403.9-404.7 (baseline
# median). Reading the $SIGMA variances (77, 24.2) as SDs widens the tails by
# well over 50 ms; a mis-transcribed baseline or increase moves the median.
stopifnot(
  all(on_trt$p50 > 410 - 5 & on_trt$p50 < 424 + 5),
  all(on_trt$p025 > 380 - 10 & on_trt$p025 < 395 + 10),
  all(on_trt$p975 > 443 - 10 & on_trt$p975 < 458 + 10),
  abs(baseline$p50 - 404) < 6
)
```

The paper also notes that "participants with a low baseline QTcTBT typically had
a longer QTcTBT prolongation on treatment", which is the -0.49 correlation
between the baseline and increase random effects. The individual predictions
show it:

```{r baseline-vs-increase}
indiv <- sim |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(baseline = QTcTBT[time == 0], increase = QTcTBT[time == 84] - QTcTBT[time == 0])
r <- cor(indiv$baseline, indiv$increase)
r
# Sex and age add uncorrelated spread to the baseline, so the correlation of
# the predictions sits a little closer to zero than -0.49.
stopifnot(r < -0.2)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Step placed at day 10.** Text S1 switches the increase on at
  `TIME.GT.10` with TIME in days, and that is what the model does. The Results
  describe the step as "implemented between baseline and Week 1", and the VPC of
  Figure 3 already shows the increase at the week-1 visit, which a day-7 ECG
  would fall before under the code. The paper does not give the exact visit
  days. Under the code a week-1 ECG on day 7 is predicted at baseline; from day
  11 the two readings agree. The VPC above is therefore compared from week 2.
* **Residual error correlation within an ECG timepoint.** Text S1 uses the L2
  data item so that the per-timepoint error `ERR(1)` is shared by the triplicate
  readings of one timepoint, while each replicate has its own `ERR(2-4)`
  (common variance, `$SIGMA BLOCK(1) SAME`). rxode2 has no L2 structure; the
  model gives the marginal SD of a single reading,
  `sqrt((addSd * exp(eta_re_add))^2 + (addSdRepl * exp(eta_re_repl))^2)`, which is
  exact for single readings (most of the data) but treats triplicate readings
  as independent.
* **Missing M2 exposure.** Text S1 imputes a missing M2 AUC0-24 to the
  10.54 mg*h/L median; supply 10.54 for subjects without one.
* **QTcF model values.** Table S4 prints only typical values and CV%; its
  omegas were obtained by inverting the CV convention verified above against the
  QTcTBT model. The QTcF model shares the QTcTBT model's structure, step day and
  covariate centring, as the paper describes it as the same model refitted to
  QTcF; it prints no separate code.
* **RR units in the QTcTBT formula.** The paper writes RR in ms; the
  correction is used with RR in seconds (above).
* **Virtual cohort.** Age and M2 exposure distributions are approximations of
  Table 1 and Tables S5-S6; the baseline in the simulation is a single reading,
  whereas the trials averaged three pre-treatment ECGs.
